rv.q: SHUCKED hits that rare, sweet spot: warm, funny and a little bit bawdy, with butter-smooth vocals and just the right pinch of saltiness.
What makes SHUCKED so irresistibly appealing even to the most cynical of theatregoers is its sly, self-aware humor wrapped around a sincere emotional core.
The singing, dancing, acting, comic timing and preposterous storytelling, all work well.
Basically, this was delightful, corny fun (yeah, I had to) from beginning to end and should not be missed.
“Shucked” is, simply put, arguably the funniest comedy I have ever seen in a theater.
Seriously, this is the funniest new musical to come around to the Bay Area in ages.

The jokes, as well as the songs, carry the show into the realm of something special, and it does what so many shows do not do: It returns the word comedy to the honorific “Musical Comedy,” which has almost gotten lost in recent years.
With its satisfying element, it was easy to get shucked up at this — sorry, y'all — a-maize-ing show.

As someone who’s seen her fair share of Broadway productions, I can confidently say this corny (pun absolutely intended) musical is one of the freshest, funniest shows to hit the road in recent memory.
Shucked isn't here to change the world or unlock any deeper truths. But for two and a half hours, it'll make you laugh, maybe cry, definitely tap your toes.
“Shucked,” on a Boston stop through April 20 of its North American tour, made me laugh.
If you enjoy a good laugh or a few dozen of them along with a good story filled with song, dance and romance, then this one is for you.
It's been a while since I've enjoyed a touring Broadway musical this much.
This show's apolitical, outrageously silly humor and the warmth of its open-hearted characters make "Shucked"
Puns aplenty come flying at you like popcorn kernels, and the maize malapropisms will have you all ears.
If you liked any of those shows, you’ll like SHUCKED.
"Shucked" made me laugh. A lot, and often in spite of better judgment at the most groan-worthy moments in this rapid-fire script of jokes, puns and double entendres.
You won’t like “Shucked” if you can’t get a little corny with it.
"Shucked" offers the Broadway equivalent of a solid popcorn flick: an escapist romp through a maze of love, laughs and corn.
Laughter, no matter the reason, almost always gives the disheartened a ray of hope.
There’s a linguistic surprise—or two or three or four—on every page.
"Shucked" is a sharply funny satire packed with innuendo and lightning-fast one-liners.
Come for the music, stay for the puns and pick up a harmless souvenir or two at “Shucked.”
I had a brainlessly good time I can scarcely remember two hours later, as I write this.
But that style of Americana vaudeville depends on a certain tone and timing, which this show only intermittently achieved for me during its two-and-a-half-hour run.

cn.t: Critics find this pun-packed musical comedy relentlessly corny but surprisingly funny, with joke density and country-bluegrass charm winning over most reviewers despite groan-worthy humor and a thin plot.
